svg.aria-label: At day 16, 11:30, launchd runs run.sh, which invokes claude -p as the orchestrating agent with a fixed MCP allowlist. The agent lane searches Gmail for the NFS-e receipt (read-only), extracts the BRL amount, shells to ptax.py for the BCB PTAX rate, and applies a USD 20 cap that is enforced only in the agent's procedure text, not in code — a soft gate. The agent then shells to enviar_dedicado.py, which first checks enviados.json for the current month (a hard idempotency gate) before touching the browser. If the session is alive, it fills the Google Form via the dedicated Chrome profile, uploads the receipt through the Google Picker iframe, and only submits once anexo_presente confirms the file chip actually appears — a second hard gate. A retired script, enviar_perfil_real.py, once used the real personal Chrome profile and logged the operator out of everything in July 2026; it is drawn as a dead, disconnected path. If parede_de_login detects a Google sign-in wall, the run stops, emits SESSAO_EXPIRADA, DMs the operator on Slack instead of failing silently, and waits on a manual login_dedicado.py recovery that never types a password and confirms session cookies both live and on disk. On a successful submission the agent notifies the approver on Slack and logs a completed event on Google Calendar.
